notes.decision: Translated 'the Rising' from root ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise, stand up.' The five 'noetic ones of the Rising' parallel the cosmic Ascent — the upward-directional principle of the Manichaean light system. Alternative readings 'the Strife/Resurrection' possible but less anchored in immediate context.

'The seven sons of the First Man' — likely the Five Sons + Call (ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ) + Hearing (ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ) yielding seven, since the present passage explicitly counts 5 noetic + Call + Hearing = 7. ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡⲧ = ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ + nominalizing -ⲧ, taken as the standard 'First (Man)' (ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ).
Variant orthography of ⲡⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ 'the Youth' — same Manichaean Christological epithet (cf. accumulated vocabulary). Possibly metathesis or Lycopolitan dialectal alternation.

Translated 'torpor' (state of sluggish neglect / oblivion-sleep) — recurs five times on this page in pairing with ⲕⲣⲁϥ 'guile' (lines 11, 15, 26, 31) and once in the sea (l.23 'great torpor'). Both contexts fit a Manichaean νωθρία/forgetfulness-sleep cast by matter. Etymology unclear; may relate to ⲃⲱϣ 'be ignorant/forget' or to a dialectal abstract for 'lapse.' Same translation maintained throughout for consistency.
Greek φερέκατοχος 'bearer/holder of the captives' — Manichaean technical figure functioning as warden of the bound powers. Retained in transliteration to preserve the technical title.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲉⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'the prison.' Confirmed by the immediately following ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲏⲣ 'of the bound ones' — standard Coptic carceral collocation. Distinct from ⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'destruction' that appears nearby (line 31).

Read as 'darkness/blackness' (variant of ⲱⲕⲙ̄ / Sah. ⲕⲁⲕⲉ-related). Phrase 'the entire darkness of Death' fits standard Manichaean cosmological idiom for the totality of the Dark Realm bound by the Pillar.
Verb root unidentified; editor's restoration ϣⲉ may indicate ⲧⲟⲩⲣⲁϣⲉ 'cause to rejoice' (improbable in context) or a verb of rousing/agitation. Translation left blank, flagged for parallel research.
Read as ⲁⲥⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ 'she/it was molded/established' (with intrusive ⲣ), 3sg.f. perfect of ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ 'shape, fashion' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛ̄ⲕ 'formation'). Subject is matter/Hyle as cosmic mother.

Tentatively 'the labor' from ⲃⲱⲕⲉ/ⲃⲁⲕⲉ 'work, toil.' Could alternatively be 'the city' (ⲃⲁⲕⲓ) or 'the maidservant.' Context (third firmament, encampment of the Great King of Honor) underdetermined. Flagged for parallels.
Read as 'disturbance, agitation' from ⲟⲩⲱϣ-stem (cf. ⲟⲩⲱϣⲣ̄ 'disturb, scatter'). Pairs naturally with 'guile' and 'torpor' as the three traits arising in the Watchers' encampment.

Translated 'the irons' as the Watchers' revealed metallurgical secrets — direct echo of the Enochic tradition where the fallen Watchers teach humanity the working of iron and the mysteries of heaven. The pairing 'opened the irons / disclosed the mysteries' confirms the Enochic reception in Manichaean cosmography.

Lexeme of uncertain identity opening a new section after 'leer.' Possibly the feminine of ⲡⲁⲗⲁⲙⲁⲥ 'the contriver' (already in vocabulary), or a Greek-derived term (ταλαμᾶς?), or a proper name. Left transliterated as 'Talamas' pending parallels.
